  "elsewhere_quote": "Since both cases lead to a contradiction when $c \\ne e$, we must have $c = e$. Hence all positive values of $d$ coincide; there exists $c \\ge 0$ such that\n$$\nd(x) \\in \\{0, c\\} \\quad \\forall x > 0. \\qquad (6)\n$$",
  "status_as_written": "established",
  "repair_distance": "none",
  "explanation": "The displayed coefficient outside the square is actually $2c^2-4ce+2c(x_0-y_0)$, so (5), with an unrestricted $O(n+m)$ remainder, has no standalone sign content. The objection is locally correct. However, the subsequent rational and irrational cases impose $em=cn$ or $em=cn+O(1)$; direct substitution into the exact expression preceding (5) then gives $4c(c-e)n+O(1)$. Swapping the two orbits handles the opposite sign. Thus the later case argument does establish that all positive deviations are equal despite the uninformative display."
